_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE PATH-SCOPE LAWS ARE NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/citation-path-scope.sweep.json
WHAT IT IS ABOUT. `validate-code-refs --paths <file>...` is SCE lift-request
4-B: a run narrowed to the files a commit touched, judging the axes that one
file plus the store can decide, and SAYING SO about the ones it cannot. Six
tests in `validate_code_refs_path_scope.rs` and three in `code_refs.rs` state
those laws, and they shipped green — which says the laws hold and says
nothing about whether they could break. Each injection below breaks ONE READ
and names the tests that must go red for it.
SCOPE IS THE WHOLE WORKSPACE. The edits land in `mnemosyne-validate` and in
`mnemosyne-cli`, and Round 1139 measured what a narrower run costs: under
`-p mnemosyne-cli` the EDITED CRATE'S OWN SUITE never runs, so a law its unit
tests already guard and a law nothing guards come back as the same red set.
`--workspace` is the widest reading of the population that can go red.
THE RED SETS HERE ARE PREDICTIONS AND ARE NOT YET MEASURED, so the manifest
claims `at-least` (the default) rather than Round 1140's `exhaustive`. The
sweep's CONTROL has run on this tree — 1858 passed, 0 failed, 159 targets —
and no injection has. Each `expect_red` below is what the author expects to
go red and says nothing about the rest, which is the only honest reading
for a red set nobody has counted. Promoting this file to `exhaustive` takes
one full run of it and replacing every list with what that run reported;
the interesting claims — 'breaking the null-vs-zero rule reddens five
suites, breaking the scope filter reddens a different four' — are prose
until then.
THE ONE PREDICTION WORTH READING AHEAD OF THE RUN: the axis-verdict map is
read by the scan (as its skip conditions) and by the report (as its
`not_judged` list), and injection `the-report-stops-naming-the-axes-it-
skipped` cuts only the second reader. If the two had drifted into separate
derivations, that injection would redden nothing at all.

injections.name: the-scope-stops-narrowing-the-read-set
injections.why: the scope exists to make the run read fewer files; with the filter gone a scoped run answers about the whole tree while still calling itself scoped, which is the equality law's exact negation

injections.name: a-scoped-run-judges-the-spec-side-anyway
injections.why: the spec-side axes ask whether a store claim has a witness ANYWHERE; judged against a partial read set every binding outside the scope looks unwitnessed, so this is the false-reject a consumer's hook would eat

edits.to: } else if false && scoped && axis.side() == AuditSide::Spec {

injections.name: the-report-stops-naming-the-axes-it-skipped
injections.why: an axis nobody judged and an axis that found nothing print the same silence; the naming is the whole difference, and three suites beyond the scope tests read it

injections.name: an-axis-nobody-measured-publishes-a-zero
injections.why: this is the defect in its original form — three modes printed `0` for an axis they structurally skip, and `0` is the answer a judged-and-clean axis gives; the rejection message is downstream of the same map, so it goes back to printing the zero too

injections.name: a-file-this-gate-never-reads-is-filed-as-absent
injections.why: 'no configured path covers it' and 'it is not on disk' are two different pieces of news for a hook handing over a changed-file list, and only one of them is the consumer's typo

injections.name: the-narrowing-vanishes-from-the-human-report
injections.why: the consumer reads a terminal; a scoped run whose short violation list is the only evidence of narrowing looks exactly like a clean whole-tree run

injections.name: the-resolver-goes-back-to-the-disk
injections.why: the point of passing the source is that the symbol answer comes from the bytes the citation was extracted from; a plugin that reads the path again has its own copy, and two reads of one file can disagree

injections.name: the-file-is-put-to-the-resolver-one-citation-at-a-time
injections.why: this is the 108.9-second defect itself: the demand is batched per file, and a call that carries only the first line is the shape the batching replaced

injections.name: the-census-prices-every-bound-citation-instead-of-the-checked-ones
injections.why: a census that counts `cited and bound` rather than `records a symbol` overstates the axis's cost, and the consumer's payoff estimate is a division by exactly this number

injections.name: the-scan-emits-what-the-verdict-map-says-it-skipped
injections.why: the run self-checks that a not-judged axis emitted nothing, and a self-check with no reader is the shape this project keeps finding; here the map still says `not judged` while step 3 runs, so the check must stop the run rather than let a consistent-looking report out
